components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid Working Blue action button, the only button style that carries brand color.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #4584ed; color: #fff; padding: 13px 26px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.15s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2d65c4; transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(69,132,237,0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4584ed; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary / Ghost Button
components.description: Bordered, transparent-background button for secondary actions (Cancel, toolbar actions).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #5f6368; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #4584ed; color: #4584ed; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill badge with a tinted background, solid-color text, and a leading dot. One instance shown in the 'approved' state.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: rgba(34,197,94,0.1); color: #22c55e; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 100px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-dot { width: 5px; height: 5px; border-radius: 50%; background: #22c55e; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat resting card with a hairline border, lifting to a shadow on hover when it's clickable.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px; transition: transform 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s, border-color 0.3s; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.04); border-color: rgba(69,132,237,0.22); } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Roboto Slab', serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; color: #2f2f2f; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 11px; color: #5f6368; }

narrative.overview: HR staff open this product dozens of times a day to make real decisions about real people. The system is built like a briefing room, not a showroom: evidence laid out clearly, scored and labeled, ready for a fast and confident call. Nothing here performs for a viewer, every score circle, badge, and panel exists to answer one question (can I trust this candidate's file enough to act on it right now) as fast as possible. The palette stays restrained on purpose: a single blue carries interaction and identity, neutrals do the rest, and saturated color is reserved entirely for status and score meaning so color is always information, never decoration.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (#4584ed) carries all interactive/brand meaning; saturated color elsewhere is reserved for status and score semantics only
Heavy, tight-tracked slab-serif display type paired with a plain system sans body
Evidence-first component design: scores are always shown with their reasoning, never as a bare number
Elevation is a response to interaction (hover lift + shadow), not ambient decoration
Every destructive or blocking action routes through a real modal component; native confirm()/alert()/prompt() never appear

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Working Blue is the only color allowed to mean "click here" or "this is the brand." Every other saturated color on screen means something about candidate/application state, and only that.

rules.name: The Tinted Fill Rule
rules.body: A status or score color never appears as a large solid fill. It appears as a small dot, text, a thin ring stroke, or a background tint at ~10% opacity.

rules.name: The Density Rule
rules.body: Body copy runs small (12.5-13px) and tight (1.5-1.6 line-height) everywhere data needs to be scanned. This is a working tool used all day, not a marketing page.

rules.name: The Earned Elevation Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats just to look premium. A shadow either responds to interaction (hover, focus) or exists because the element genuinely sits above the page (modal, dropdown, toast).

dos: Do keep Working Blue as the only color that means "interactive"
Do pair every score or AI verdict with its reasoning visible nearby
Do use flat cards with hairline borders at rest, promoting to shadow + lift only on hover or genuine elevation
Do reuse the existing Score Circle, StatusBadge, and ConfirmDialog components rather than inventing parallel one-off styles
Do keep body copy dense - this is a working tool used all day, not a marketing page
donts: Don't introduce the vibrant purple/blue gradient SaaS look - no gradient header banners, no glassmorphic cards floating over saturated color, no heavily saturated donut charts as decoration
Don't let this read as a generic admin-dashboard template - no interchangeable icon-in-a-circle stat cards, no stock dashboard-kit identity
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items
Don't use gradient text anywhere in the product UI
Don't use a native confirm(), alert(), or prompt() anywhere
Don't use emojis anywhere in the product UI
Don't apply a static drop shadow to a card or panel that isn't interactive or genuinely elevated
